pr_title: sqlmigrations: fix handling of mutations in schema change job migration
pr_body:
The migration for schema change jobs assumed that a table descriptor's
`MutationJobs` were always synced with `Mutations`, so we were indexing
into `Mutations` with the `MutationJobs` index. In practice, if this
assumption doesn't hold due to some previous buggy schema change, we
risk crashing with an out of bounds error or looking up the wrong
mutation. This PR adds a step to find the mutation with the expected ID
and mark the job as failed if the mutation doesn't exist.

Fixes #48786.

Release note (bug fix): Fix a problem introduced in v20.1.0 where the
migration for ongoing schema change jobs would cause the node to panic
with an index out of bounds error, upon encountering a malformed table
descriptor with no schema change mutation corresponding to the job to be
migrated.

comments:
This could well be us that caused the panic & raised this issue.

Not sure how, but if we can be of any help in debugging this with you let me know.

`MutationJobs` and `Mutations` should never be out of sync on the table descriptor, so I'm concerned about how this table got into a state where there's a job in `MutationJobs` but no mutation. But we should really be more defensive in handling it.

@rcrowe Thanks for letting us know. What symptoms are you seeing on your cluster? Are nodes crash-looping with an interval of ~10s of seconds (which seems to be what the Sentry report is indicating)? If you're willing to send us the logs from the cluster, it would be very useful.

As for how to fix this: I don't think the migration should try to clean up invalid state on the table descriptor itself. If we find a `MutationJob` with no mutation, as in this case, we should just mark the job as failed.

The theoretical existence of mutations without `MutationJob`s is a tricker case (though, after searching through the issues for the error, it doesn't look like it's ever been reported). I think in 19.2 this would have led to an endlessly failing schema change (and all other schema changes blocked) when we failed to find the job for the mutation. In 20.1, something similar would happen, in that the mutation would never get executed and all further schema changes would be blocked. In this case, there's nothing for the migration to do except leave the table descriptor alone.

Thanks @davidsbond. I think those logs are at `WARNING` level; would you be able to provide `INFO`-level logs, and preferably with `--vmodule=migrations=2,registry=2,schema_changer=2` in the flags to `cockroach start`? (If you'd prefer to not post logs on GitHub, you can open a ticket on https://support.cockroachlabs.com/ and attach the logs.)

This bug can be triggered if there was a schema change in progress during the upgrade to 20.1.0, and the table metadata descriptor itself was in some invalid state (the potential root cause of this isn't clear to me). Did you have any schema changes running during the upgrade, and if so, could you let us know what those schema changes were? It'd also be useful to know if you've seen any other unexpected/buggy behavior related to the table that schema changes were being run on.

I believe there should be an `INFO` log statement `job <some job id>: undergoing schema change job migration` immediately before the crash for this particular job. If you can manage to run any queries on the cluster before it crashes, you can get the specific job with that ID from the output of `select * from crdb_internal.jobs` or from the admin UI, to narrow down the specific schema change. (Logging flags are documented at https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v20.1/debug-and-error-logs.html.)

Unfortunately I don't think there's any immediate mitigation aside from restoring from a backup. The crash will be fixed in 20.1.1, released within the next few weeks. I should have #48823 merged and backported to the 20.1 branch today or tomorrow, so another option is building a binary from the 20.1 branch before 20.1.1 becomes available.

I'm going to reopen this for now since there's still ongoing discussion about the root cause. It's possible the root cause of the malformed descriptor/job is not closely related to the panic itself, but if we determine that then we can open a separate issue at that point.
Hi all, my team has managed to dump out the jobs table as requested, due to mentions of schema, I've used the support link shared above to send them over. Thanks for your help!

@daylerees I've responded on the ticket. We can keep discussion specific to your cluster on the ticket if you'd prefer.

Based on the output of `crdb_internal.jobs`, the probable root cause is a leftover `pending` job from before the upgrade that was never properly cleaned up, which is for some reason accompanied by a dangling `MutationJob` on the table descriptor. This is a bug (which should be fixed in 20.1 with the new schema change jobs), but this leftover job state shouldn't cause other problems by itself. So it does seem so far that the root cause isn't something caused by the 20.1 upgrade but rather some preexisting bad state.
I've opened https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/49098 to track the invalid leftover job state separately. I'll close this issue since the crash itself is fixed.
